title: How to preserve okra
seoTitle: How to Freeze, Pickle and Can Okra Safely
description: Freeze okra after a 3 or 4 minute blanch, pickle it with a tested dilled okra recipe, or pressure can it. Safe, tested steps for your harvest.
summary: Freeze okra after blanching it for 3 to 4 minutes, or pickle it with a tested recipe and a boiling-water canner. Plain okra can only be canned in a pressure canner. Fresh pods keep only a few days, so preserve them soon after picking.

heroImage.alt: A hand holding a wide-mouth glass jar packed with whole pickled okra pods in brine, with garlic at the bottom.

socialImage.alt: How to preserve okra card with a photo of a jar of homemade pickled okra.

intro: A healthy okra patch can give you more pods than you can eat. Freezing and pickling keep that summer harvest going all year.
For picking and storing fresh pods, start with [how to harvest okra](/okra/how-to-harvest-okra).

items: Fresh: refrigerate unwashed and use within a few days
Freeze: blanch small pods 3 minutes, large pods 4
Pickle: follow a tested recipe and process the jars
Can plain okra: pressure canner only

blocks.text: Fresh okra keeps best at [45°F to 50°F in a moist environment](https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/how-to-grow-okra-in-south-carolina-including-planting-dates-watering-fertilizing-ratooning-pest-management-and-harvesting-tips-for-healthy-pod-production/). Don't wash the pods until you're ready to use them, since washing speeds up decay. Clemson Extension says well-handled pods can last up to seven days in the refrigerator, but they're at their best in the first few days, so preserve extras soon after picking.
Freezing is the simplest way to keep okra. These steps follow the [National Center for Home Food Preservation](https://nchfp.uga.edu/how/freeze/vegetable/freezing-okra/).

items: Pick young, tender pods. Sort them into small pods, 4 inches or under, and large pods.
Wash the pods and trim off the stems, without cutting into the seed cells.
Blanch in boiling water: 3 minutes for small pods, 4 minutes for large pods.
Cool the pods promptly and drain.
Leave them whole or slice them crosswise, pack into freezer containers or bags with 1/2 inch of headspace, seal and freeze.

blocks.title: Freezing okra for frying
blocks.text: After blanching and cooling, slice the pods crosswise and coat the slices in cornmeal or flour. Spread them in a single layer on a tray and freeze just until firm, then pack them into containers with 1/2 inch of headspace. They go straight from the freezer to the pan.

This is the [National Center for Home Food Preservation's tested Pickled Dilled Okra recipe](https://nchfp.uga.edu/how/pickle/vegetable-pickles/pickled-dilled-okra/), processed in a boiling-water canner. It makes 8 to 9 pints.

items: 7 pounds small okra pods
6 small hot peppers
4 teaspoons dill seed
8 to 9 garlic cloves
2/3 cup canning or pickling salt
6 cups water
6 cups vinegar (5% acidity)
Wash and trim the okra. Pack the pods firmly into clean pint jars, leaving 1/2 inch of headspace, and add 1 garlic clove to each jar.
Bring the salt, hot peppers, dill seed, water and vinegar to a boil in a large saucepan.
Pour the hot brine over the okra, leaving 1/2 inch of headspace.
Put on the lids and process the jars in a boiling-water canner for the time below.

blocks.caption: Boiling-water canner processing time for pint jars

blocks.title: Keep it safe
blocks.text: Don't change the amounts of vinegar, water or okra, and only use vinegar labeled 5% acidity. The National Center notes that a [tested, uniform level of acid](https://nchfp.uga.edu/how/pickle/general-information-pickling/general-information-on-pickling/) is what keeps pickles safe. The tested recipe gives times for pint jars only.

Plain okra, without vinegar, isn't acidic enough for a boiling-water canner. It has to be [processed in a pressure canner](https://nchfp.uga.edu/how/can/canning-vegetables-and-vegetable-products/okra/), following the National Center's times for your canner type and elevation. If you don't have a pressure canner, freeze or pickle it instead.

faq.question: Do you have to blanch okra before freezing?
faq.answer: Yes. The National Center for Home Food Preservation blanches small pods for 3 minutes and large pods for 4, then cools them right away before packing and freezing.

faq.question: Can you can okra in a water bath?
faq.answer: Only as pickles. A tested pickled okra recipe uses enough vinegar for a boiling-water canner. Plain okra has to be pressure canned.

faq.question: How long does fresh okra last in the fridge?
faq.answer: Up to about a week if it's stored unwashed, but it's best in the first few days. Preserve extra pods soon after picking.

faq.question: Can I use quart jars for pickled okra?
faq.answer: The tested Pickled Dilled Okra recipe only gives processing times for pint jars, so use pints when canning it.
